It’s been, I’d say, several months now that things have felt…off. My wife keeps telling me she’s worried about how I’m eating when I’m home from a trip. I’ll come back from a voyage and it’s like a switch flips—late at night I’ll raid the galley or the kitchen and just keep going. Not just a snack; I’ll put away enough for three people in maybe half an hour. I don’t really stop until my stomach feels tight and painful, like after a bad storm when the ship’s listing and you’ve overdone it on coffee.

I usually do it when everyone’s asleep. I’m embarrassed by how much I’m shoveling in, so I wait until I’m alone in the mess or the kitchen. If I hear footsteps, I’ll shove things back in the cupboard like I’ve been caught stealing.

At the same time, there are stretches where I’m more wired than usual—talking fast with the crew, sleeping less, making big plans about routes and side businesses. Then it kind of burns out, and I’m left feeling heavy and ashamed, especially about these eating bouts. I’m not sure what’s normal anymore.

I usually ask the aides if I can bring the food back to my room instead of eating in the dining hall. I don’t like people watching me when I eat like that; I feel ashamed, like they’ll think I’m greedy or have no self-control.

Around those same times, I also get these spells where I’m oddly “revved up” for someone my age. I talk more, feel like I have extra pep, and want to organize things or stay up later than I should.
